[[File:Small hexagrammic hexecontahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a small hexagrammic hexecontahedron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''small hexagrammic hexecontahedron''' is a nonconvex [[Isohedral figure|isohedral]] [[polyhedron]]. It is the [[Dual polyhedron|dual]] of the [[small retrosnub icosicosidodecahedron]]. It is partially [[degeneracy (mathematics)|degenerate]], having coincident [[Vertex (geometry)|vertices]], as its dual has coplanar triangular faces.

==Geometry==

Its faces are hexagonal stars  with two short and four long edges. Denoting the [[golden ratio]] by <math>\phi</math> and putting <math>\xi = \frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{1+4\phi}\approx 0.933\,380\,199\,59</math>, the stars have five equal angles of <math>\arccos(\xi)\approx 21.031\,988\,967\,51^{\circ}</math> and one of <math>360^{\circ}-\arccos(\phi^{-2}\xi-\phi^{-1})\approx 254.840\,055\,162\,43^{\circ}</math>. Each face has four long and two short edges. The ratio between the edge lengths is 
:<math>1/2 -1/2\times\sqrt{(1-\xi)/(\phi^{3}-\xi)}\approx 0.428\,986\,992\,12</math>. 
The [[dihedral angle]] equals <math>\arccos(\xi/(1+\xi))\approx 61.133\,452\,273\,64^{\circ}</math>. Part of each face is inside the solid, hence is not visible in solid models.
